claims.statement: From 18 February 2027, each EV battery, light-means-of-transport battery, and industrial battery above 2 kWh placed on the market or put into service must have a battery passport.
The battery passport uses a decentralised model in which the responsible economic operator maintains detailed data, including information relevant to performance, repair, reuse, and recycling.
The Commission's DPP Registry became operational on 20 July 2026, and August 2026 battery guidance maps 71 data points across covered battery categories.

contrary_evidence: Battery and DPP software vendors are already entering the market, and the Commission registry plus standards lower the barrier to basic passport issuance.
The responsible economic operator, not the component supplier, owns the core obligation, limiting the initial buyer set.

economics.acquisition_route: Pilot 100-500 stationary packs with one Polish assembler or importer and the family installer, then bundle via inverter distributors and second-life workshops
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 350000 active passports at 18 PLN annual blended revenue plus 60 operator accounts at 60000 PLN gives 9.9m PLN recurring revenue; at 28% EBITDA, 4x EBITDA, and 60% founder ownership, equity could exceed 6.6m PLN in years 6-9. Validate issuance volume, churn, and dilution needs; do not double-count retained cash.
economics.founder_time: 3-5 hours per day for one stationary-storage segment; use standards/security contractors and avoid hardware manufacturing
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 86-94% for hosting and standard events; BMS integrations and manual legacy-data work priced as setup projects
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 12-24 months because integrations precede volume; target two anchor operators paying at least 40000 PLN setup plus annual minimums
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 18-60 PLN issuance plus 8-24 PLN per battery per year, with portfolio minimums of 18000 PLN and premium health/residual-value APIs
economics.retention_or_repeat: The passport and service history must persist for the battery's life; changing custodian risks broken links, lost permissions, and incomplete residual-value evidence

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A longitudinal battery identity graph combining model, use, repair, health, transfer, repurposing, and recycling events improves residual-value models and makes the custodian harder to replace
fingerprint.customer: EU industrial and home-storage battery assemblers, importers, repurposers, second-life operators, fleet owners, and their downstream service partners
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Embed with storage assemblers, inverter and battery distributors, solar installers, diagnostic workshops, insurers, leasing providers, and recyclers; every asset creates downstream participant invitations
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: DPP registry handoff, access-controlled passport hosting, data-collection workflows, service and health events, responsibility transfer, and residual-value evidence API
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The responsible economic operator pays per passport at placement and an annual custody fee; later owners, financiers, or fleets pay for portfolio verification and health history
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A covered battery is placed on the market, put into service, repaired, transferred, evaluated for second life, repurposed, or sent for recycling and its passport must remain coherent

founder_fit: Direct renewable-energy design access through the parents' company
Strong match to quantified asset health, data science, and longevity-style monitoring
Software-only scope avoids capital-heavy battery inventory
Can begin part-time with one assembler, although security and standards expertise must be contracted
risks: Long-lived regulated data hosting imposes security, uptime, interoperability, and continuity obligations.
Battery-management-system integrations may be proprietary and expensive.
A large assembler may select a global DPP platform before a Poland-first product matures.

structure.control_point: the unique registered battery passport required at market placement and maintained through the asset's circular lifecycle
structure.critical_dependency: trusted long-term hosting, correct access rights, and data feeds from battery-management systems and responsible economic operators

thesis: Create battery-passport infrastructure specifically for European stationary storage assemblers, importers, repurposers, and second-life operators using industrial packs above 2 kWh. The product registers the unique identifier, hosts permissioned passport data, collects model and individual-use fields, and preserves the chain of responsibility when a pack is repaired, remanufactured, repurposed, financed, insured, or transferred. Start with Polish solar-storage installers and battery diagnostic/repurposing workshops, using the founder's family renewable business for workflow access, then distribute through inverter distributors, insurers, leasing firms, and recyclers. The moat is not QR generation but a longitudinal asset identity, health, service, ownership, and residual-value graph that becomes useful to every later participant.
title: Second-Life Battery Passport Custodian
uncertainties: Stationary-storage passport volumes reachable through Polish and regional channels
Legal procedure and liability for changing custodians or transferring responsibility after repurposing
Whether residual-value analytics can be offered using legitimately accessible passport and BMS data
